legend: Every December, VK traditionally holds an event for its employees named "Secret Santa". Here's how it happens.

n%%ZSMJ0%% employees numbered from 1%%ZSMJ1%% to n%%ZSMJ2%% take part in the event. Each employee i%%ZSMJ3%% is assigned a different employee bi%%ZSMJ4%%, to which employee i%%ZSMJ5%% has to make a new year gift. Each employee is assigned to exactly one other employee, and nobody is assigned to themselves (but two employees may be assigned to each other). Formally, all bi%%ZSMJ6%% must be distinct integers between 1%%ZSMJ7%% and n%%ZSMJ8%%, and for any i%%ZSMJ9%%, bi≠i%%ZSMJ10%% must hold.

The assignment is usually generated randomly. This year, as an experiment, all event participants have been asked who they wish to make a gift to. Each employee i%%ZSMJ11%% has said that they wish to make a gift to employee ai%%ZSMJ12%%.
Find a valid assignment b%%ZSMJ13%% that maximizes the number of fulfilled wishes of the employees.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t%%ZSMJ14%% (1≤t≤105%%ZSMJ15%%). Description of the test cases follows.
Each test case consists of two lines. The first line contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ16%% (2≤n≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ17%%) — the number of participants of the event.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ18%% integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ19%% (1≤ai≤n%%ZSMJ20%%; ai≠i%%ZSMJ21%%) — wishes of the employees in order from 1%%ZSMJ22%% to n%%ZSMJ23%%.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ24%% over all test cases does not exceed 2⋅105%%ZSMJ25%%.
output: For each test case, print two lines.
In the first line, print a single integer k%%ZSMJ26%% (0≤k≤n%%ZSMJ27%%) — the number of fulfilled wishes in your assignment.
In the second line, print n%%ZSMJ28%% distinct integers b1,b2,…,bn%%ZSMJ29%% (1≤bi≤n%%ZSMJ30%%; bi≠i%%ZSMJ31%%) — the numbers of employees assigned to employees 1,2,…,n%%ZSMJ32%%.
k%%ZSMJ33%% must be equal to the number of values of i%%ZSMJ34%% such that ai=bi%%ZSMJ35%%, and must be as large as possible. If there are multiple answers, print any.
note: In the first test case, two valid assignments exist: [3,1,2]%%ZSMJ36%% and [2,3,1]%%ZSMJ37%%. The former assignment fulfills two wishes, while the latter assignment fulfills only one. Therefore, k=2%%ZSMJ38%%, and the only correct answer is [3,1,2]%%ZSMJ39%%.
